clue.text: Cholmondeley's character in soup (car driven — horn out of order)

indicators.note: being in the soup is being in a mess, so these letters are jumbled
something out of order is disarranged, a second signal that the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A motorist is in trouble because the car's horn has broken while driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in soup' and 'out of order' both signal that the thirteen letters of CAR DRIVEN HORN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Cholmondeley, the Victorian novelist, created a figure of this name in her fiction.

clue.text: Dickensian greengrocer who answered to the gentleman in black

definitions.meaning: a tradesman sworn as a juror in the Bardell v Pickwick trial in The Pickwick Papers

definitions.text: who answered to the gentleman in black
definitions.meaning: the court official in black calls the jurors' names, and this juror replied to his

explanation.walkthrough: In The Pickwick Papers the jury is called over by a gentleman in black; this greengrocer is the juror who answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens names this shopkeeper among the jurymen in the breach-of-promise case against Mr Pickwick.

clue.text: Church residence for goddess

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An ecclesiastical house is dedicated to a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity of agriculture and harvests bears this name.

clue.text: Reason for Boileau-Narcejac's detective being reluctant to reach the heights

definitions.text: Reason for Boileau-Narcejac's detective being reluctant to reach the heights

parts.words: Reason for Boileau-Narcejac's detective being reluctant to reach the heights
parts.note: the French writing duo's novel became Hitchcock's Vertigo, whose detective has a crippling fear of high places

explanation.walkthrough: Boileau and Narcejac wrote D'entre les morts, filmed by Hitchcock as Vertigo; its ex-policeman hero dreads heights.
explanation.definitionFit: The clinical term means a morbid fear of heights, which is what keeps that detective off towers.

clue.text: French philosopher acted by rote, in away

parts.note: to act is to do, and did is its past tense

indicators.note: read as 'in a way', telling us the word rote is rearranged

explanation.surface: A French thinker performed his lines mechanically, as if absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acted' is DID, and 'in away' is read as 'in a way', an anagram signal; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was the Enlightenment thinker who edited the Encyclopédie.

clue.text: Sad Masonic songs

parts.note: not Freemasons' music but mournful verses by the poet William Mason, who published a collection under this title

explanation.walkthrough: 'Masonic' points not to Freemasonry but to William Mason, the 18th-century poet who issued a volume of these in 1763.
explanation.definitionFit: These are mournful poems or laments, and Mason's book of them carries the title.

clue.text: "Few little — popping away with cameras" (John Osborne, West of Suez)

definitions.text: "Few little — popping away with cameras" (John Osborne, West of Suez)

parts.words: "Few little — popping away with cameras" (John Osborne, West of Suez)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from Osborne's play: the missing word is small people, here a slangy term for Japanese tourists

explanation.walkthrough: The dash is the gap in Osborne's line; the missing word is a dated slang term for Japanese people, used by a character in West of Suez.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's line uses this short slang word for the camera-carrying tourists.

clue.text: Heresy derived from Greek sage?

parts.note: Nestor was the wise old Greek of the Iliad, but the heresy is really named after the 5th-century patriarch of Constantinople

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the joke: the heresy comes from Nestorius, not from Nestor, the sage of Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes the Christological doctrine of Nestorius, condemned at the Council of Ephesus.

clue.text: Lewis offers suitable seat for second-place runner?

definitions.text: Lewis offers suitable seat for second-place runner?

parts.words: Lewis offers suitable seat for second-place runner?
parts.note: a runner-up wins silver, so a seat of that metal suits them; C S Lewis wrote a Narnia book of this title

explanation.walkthrough: Second place earns a silver medal, so the playful seat is made of silver; it is the fourth Narnia book by C S Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: A Narnia novel by C S Lewis carries this title, which also names a fitting throne for a runner-up.

clue.text: Paper on Ammunition too stiff for writer?

definitions.text: Paper on Ammunition too stiff for writer?

parts.words: Paper on Ammunition too stiff for writer?
parts.note: thick drawing paper once used to make gun charges, perhaps too heavy for someone writing letters

explanation.walkthrough: The heavy drawing paper takes its name from its original use for wrapping gunpowder charges.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick, tough paper for drawing, named from its use in making ammunition casings.

clue.text: Festival for old writers among grandpa's childhood memories

indicators.note: the letters sit among the words grandpa's childhood, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Grandpa remembers a childhood feast that older authors described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for old writers' marks the word as archaic: it is an old name for Easter or Passover.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic word for Easter or the Passover, used by older authors.

clue.text: Greek satirist seen in a retreating attitude

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the word for attitude is read in reverse

parts.note: a pose is a bodily attitude

explanation.surface: A Greek mocker of manners is spotted backing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is a link; Aesop is usually called a fabulist, but his animal fables mock human failings.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient fabulist mocked human folly through beast tales, so satirist fits loosely.

clue.text: Precipitate idea of Maugham

definitions.meaning: to precipitate is to fall as water from the sky
the title of a famous Somerset Maugham short story about a missionary in Samoa

explanation.walkthrough: Somerset Maugham's story of that title is set during a downpour in Pago Pago.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather sense: water falling from clouds; it is also Maugham's story title.

clue.text: Pet name for Lear

parts.note: not King Lear but Edward Lear, whose beloved striped cat had this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' tempts towards Shakespeare's king; it is Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, and his tabby cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's famous cat was called this, so it was literally his pet's name.

clue.text: Lee's mastermind with history (muse quite unusual)

parts.note: a mastermind is a person of genius

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so the muse's name is rearranged

parts.note: Clio is the muse of history, as the bracketed 'muse' hints

explanation.surface: A brilliant mind steeped in the past is inspired in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: Clio, the muse of history, is shuffled by 'quite unusual' into LOCI; Vernon Lee wrote a book of essays of this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernon Lee, the English writer, published essays under this Latin title for the spirit of a place.

clue.text: Runyon's city gambler

parts.note: Damon Runyon's Nathan, who runs a floating crap game, has an American city for a surname

explanation.walkthrough: Nathan of that name, from Runyon's stories and Guys and Dolls, shares his surname with the Michigan motor city.
explanation.definitionFit: Runyon's crap-game operator Nathan bears the surname of the Michigan city.

clue.text: Meredith's unduly subjective subject

parts.note: George Meredith's novel about the self-absorbed Sir Willoughby Patterne is titled for such a person

explanation.walkthrough: George Meredith's 1879 novel takes its title from its self-centred hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person sees everything subjectively, and Meredith's novel is named for one.

clue.text: Remarkable as Hamilton's providence

definitions.meaning: the adjective qualifying providence in a well-known quoted phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'special providence' is best known from Hamlet's 'There's a special providence in the fall of a sparrow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceptional things are out of the common run, as is a providence singled out for one case.

clue.text: Lutheran principle may be seen as psi item

indicators.note: the letters of psi item may appear rearranged as something else

explanation.surface: A Lutheran tenet might look like a paranormal object.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietism was the 17th-century Lutheran movement stressing personal devotion over doctrine.

clue.text: Several feet for French person to contain wastage

indicators.note: the French word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: moi is the French first-person pronoun, me
wastage is a loss

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is asked to hold down waste.
explanation.walkthrough: French 'moi' (me) stands for a French person by a loose convention; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A molossus is a metrical foot of three long syllables, so the plural names several such feet.

clue.text: "… my words no fancy'd woes relate: / I speak from -, and the voice is Fate" (Pope, Odyssey)

definitions.text: "… my words no fancy'd woes relate: / I speak from -, and the voice is Fate" (Pope, Odyssey)

parts.words: "… my words no fancy'd woes relate: / I speak from -, and the voice is Fate" (Pope, Odyssey)
parts.note: a gap in Pope's Odyssey couplet where the speaker claims sure knowledge rather than fancy

explanation.walkthrough: The dash is the gap in Pope's translation; the speaker grounds his prophecy in sure knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope uses the word in its older sense of certain knowledge, the opposite of fancy.

clue.text: It might make Nash beg for woman hit hard in room

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
to bang is to strike hard

explanation.surface: A frustrated poet begs for a woman who was struck in a chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It might make Nash beg' is a second route: NASH BEG rearranges to the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a shebang is a hut or shed, a rough room or dwelling.

clue.text: He wrote more than one play that is inwardly no good

definitions.text: He wrote more than one play

indicators.note: the second piece goes into the first

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dramatist's works are all said to be bad at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: William Inge, the American dramatist of Picnic, wrote several plays.
explanation.definitionFit: William Inge was the American dramatist of Picnic and Bus Stop, so he wrote several stage works.

clue.text: An afternoon with William Boyd

parts.note: William Boyd's novel set partly in Manila has a colour before 'Afternoon' in its title

explanation.walkthrough: William Boyd's 1993 novel is called The Blue Afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word qualifies the afternoon of Boyd's novel title.

clue.text: Indifferent part of Dreiser's desire

definitions.meaning: unmoved by pain or pleasure, as a follower of Zeno's philosophy
the third novel of Theodore Dreiser's Trilogy of Desire

explanation.walkthrough: Theodore Dreiser's Trilogy of Desire ends with a novel under this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impassive endures without complaint, like the ancient philosophical school.

clue.text: Witchcraft starts off Banquo's exit (and haunting)

indicators.note: the starts of the next five words are taken in order

explanation.surface: Sorcery opens the scene where Banquo leaves the stage and returns as a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the first letters of OFF BANQUO'S EXIT AND HAUNTING; Banquo is murdered and haunts Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of folk magic and sorcery practised in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Melville skipper, ever unreliable

indicators.note: something unreliable cannot be counted on to keep its form, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Melville's captain was never to be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Vere commands HMS Bellipotent in Melville's Billy Budd.

clue.text: Instrument of punishment, we hear, for its rebellious occupants

indicators.note: says the word for the punishment rod is spoken, giving a same-sounding name

parts.note: a cane is a rod used for beating

explanation.surface: A rod is wielded on troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Caine Mutiny, Herman Wouk's novel, is named for the ship whose officers mutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Wouk's minesweeper is remembered for its crew's mutiny against Captain Queeg.

clue.text: Tool of Figaro's trade might have made Il Barbiere the first

definitions.text: Tool of Figaro's trade might have made Il Barbiere the first

parts.note: Figaro is a barber, and shaving lather is a barber's tool
Rossini's Il Barbiere di Siviglia is a stage work sung throughout

explanation.surface: A barber's shaving lather might have turned Rossini's comic opera into the original television serial.
explanation.walkthrough: Figaro is Rossini's barber, so his tool is lather; the whole clue imagines the opera sponsored by a detergent firm, the origin of the genre's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodramatic serial on radio or television, named for the detergent firms that sponsored them.

clue.text: Home bird seen near the bank

definitions.text: Home bird seen near the bank

parts.words: Home bird seen near the bank
parts.note: a play by William Douglas-Home is named after a brightly coloured waterside bird

explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' is William Douglas-Home, the playwright; 'Home bird' looks like a stay-at-home person.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's title names the blue riverside diving bird.
